entradas.text: Several days had passed since I ordered the investigation into my secretary, Livia Suno.
Several days had passed since the confrontation with Petr, Livia and Lucian in my office.
Lucian was still acting frosty towards me for rejecting his advice. On the other hand, both Petr and Livia were unnaturally nice to me, though they avoided speaking to each other.
Both Petr and Livia had been acting unnaturally nice to me, believing I'd let them off the hook for their affair. They seemed to be avoiding each other in the hallways, though.
I was just settling in behind my desk when Lucian knocked on my door.
"Sir, a moment of your time?"
"Of course."
entradas.menu: "Of course."

entradas.text: I motioned for him to come in. He sat and closed the door behind him.
entradas.menu: Motion for him to come in.

entradas.text: "Not now."
entradas.menu: "Not now."

entradas.text: "I'm afraid it's urgent."
He entered my office and closed the door behind him.
Lucian entered my office and closed the door behind him.

"I still believe you were wrong not to pursue an investigation into Miss Suno. However, I acknowledge my lack of concrete evidence and unorthodox information gathering method may have given you pause."
"Unorthodox? You surveilled Petr behind my back!"
entradas.menu: "Unorthodox? You surveilled Petr behind my back!"

entradas.text: "You're not going to change my mind about this."
entradas.menu: "You're not going to change my mind about this."

entradas.text: "I could have been less rude to you about it, though."
entradas.menu: "I could have been less rude to you about it, though."

entradas.text: "Perhaps."
"I feel I would be failing in my duties as a chief strategist not to give you one last piece of advice on this."
"That isn't my goal."
"I have already apologized to Mr. Vectern for the intrusion. It won't happen again."
Lucian looked me in the eye.
"Please, consider dismissing Miss Suno from her position at the palace. Just in case I am right after all."
"Are you crazy? She'll go public about the affair."
entradas.menu: "Are you crazy? She'll go public about the affair."

entradas.text: "I can't. She's so good at her job!"
entradas.menu: "I can't. She's so good at her job!"

entradas.text: "Well, she has been a distraction to Petr..."
entradas.menu: "Well, she has been a distraction to Petr..."

entradas.text: "How do I justify that to her?"
entradas.menu: "How do I justify that to her?"

entradas.text: "She slept with the vice president. Extremely unprofessional behavior."
"Her looks may be unmatched, but her skills most certainly are not."
"That might make a headline or two, but it won't sink your administration. Unlike a potential uncontrolled intelligence leak to Rumburg."
"All right. If it'll get you off my case, I'll fire her right now."
entradas.menu: "All right. If it'll get you off my case, I'll fire her."

entradas.text: "No. I won't continue to indulge your paranoid fantasies. Livia stays."
entradas.menu: "No. I won't continue to indulge your paranoid fantasies. Livia stays."

entradas.text: "Keeping Mr. Vectern around may be another mistake. But that's a conversation for another time."
"Thank you, Mr. President."
Lucian looked as if he was about to object one last time, but then smiled thinly.
"As you wish. I won't bring this up any further."
He walked out and closed the door behind him.
I called Livia into my office. She tentatively stepped in.
"What is it, Mr. President?"
I thought about how useful she'd been to me as a secretary -- and how much she knew about what I'd done.
"Nothing. Go back to work."
entradas.menu: "Nothing. Go back to work."

entradas.text: "You're fired, Livia."
entradas.menu: "You're fired, Livia."

entradas.text: "W-what? I thought we'd been over all this..."
"Um... okay. Just let me know if you need anything."
"You're making Petr too distracted to work."
entradas.menu: "You're making Petr too distracted to work."

entradas.text: Livia walked back out. Lucian looked at me in disbelief for a moment, then smiled.
"You've made your point, Mr. President. I won't trouble you with this any further."
"You're too ambitious for this job. Go get a proper university education."
entradas.menu: "You're too ambitious for this job. Go get a proper university education."

entradas.text: "I don't share Lucian's suspicions that you're a spy, but I can't take the risk that he's right."
entradas.menu: "I don't share Lucian's suspicions that you're a spy, but I can't take the risk that he's right."

entradas.text: "Your performance has been abysmal lately."
entradas.menu: "Your performance has been abysmal lately."

entradas.text: "I know that's not true."
She glared at Lucian, then at me.
"Then perhaps you should fire him."
"How prudent of you."
"That's the best you could come up with?"
"I hope you're both happy. You've ruined a woman's career simply because she acted too much like a man."
She stormed out, slamming the door behind her.
"Trust me, Mr. President, your decision was the correct one."
"I hope so."
entradas.menu: "I hope so."

entradas.text: "Stop talking. Don't make this worse than it is."
entradas.menu: "Stop talking. Don't make this worse than it is."

entradas.text: "Yes, I know."
entradas.menu: "Yes, I know."

entradas.text: I showed him out and went to brew myself a pot of coffee.
"Our security team travelled to Lachaven to speak to the owners of the pub Miss Suno named. They confirmed that one Livia Suno had worked there."
"Their description of her did not match that of your secretary."
"However, it did match that of an unidentified corpse that washed up in Lenkurg Bay two months before your inauguration."
"Oh, shit."
entradas.menu: "Oh, shit."

entradas.text: "If that was Livia Suno... who's the woman working for me?"
entradas.menu: "If that was Livia Suno... who's the woman working for me?"

entradas.text: "You mean..."
entradas.menu: "You mean..."

entradas.text: "Further investigation by our operatives in Rumburg matched Miss Suno's description to a woman named Ilana Vance, last seen graduating from Crimsrad Political Sciences Institute."
"Our whistleblower from Rumburg recognized the name Vance as belonging to a deeply embedded covert agent, although he had previously assumed it was a man."
"Recent coded transmissions from Rumburg have mentioned a deeply embedded covert agent named Vance, but our intelligence always assumed it was a man."
"How could we have missed all this?"
entradas.menu: "How could we have missed all this?"

entradas.text: "My God. You were right. I should never have doubted you."
entradas.menu: "My God. You were right. I should never have doubted you."

entradas.text: "That lying, two-faced succubus!"
entradas.menu: "That lying, two-faced succubus!"

entradas.text: "As mentioned, Miss Suno was hired without a background check. It's possible this all could have been avoided, had any of Mr. Vectern's blood flow been directed to his brain when he selected her."
"To be fair, Miss Suno was just doing her job. Your vice president, on the other hand..."
"The standard procedure would be to try Miss Suno for espionage. If we do so, it's only a matter of time before the media pieces together what happened."
"Easy. I'll get Marcel on it."
entradas.menu: "Easy. I'll get Marcel on it."

entradas.text: "You should have figured this out ages ago."
entradas.menu: "You should have figured this out ages ago."

entradas.text: "I'm happy to hear that. Now, what are you going to do, sir?"
"But none of that can be helped now. The question is, what are you going to do, sir?"
"What do you think I should do?"
entradas.menu: "What do you think I should do?"

entradas.text: "What do you mean? I'm going to murder them both."
entradas.menu: "What do you mean? I'm going to murder them both."

entradas.text: "Arrest her for espionage, of course."
entradas.menu: "Arrest her for espionage, of course."

entradas.text: "I'm going to have Petr castrated."
entradas.menu: "I'm going to have Petr castrated."

entradas.text: "Perhaps as a last resort."
Lucian lowered his voice.
Lucian stroked his beard.
"I'm going to assume you're joking."
"That would be standard procedure. However, if we do so it's only a matter of time before the media pieces together what happened."
"I wouldn't be opposed to that idea. But I meant with regards to our spy."
"I'll look like a fool for having her under my nose this entire time."
entradas.menu: "I'll look like a fool for having her under my nose this entire time."

entradas.text: "Outwitted by a woman. It won't look good."
entradas.menu: "Outwitted by a woman. It won't look good."

entradas.text: "What if there were no trial?"
entradas.menu: "What if there were no trial?"

entradas.text: "Asking Mr. Koronti for help would be advisable, but you'll still have to do a fair amount of crisis management yourself."
"With the powers granted by your emergency decree, you could certainly detain her without a trial."
"With the powers granted by your emergency decree, you could certainly detain her without a trial."
"Mr. Greiser and his men could certainly take care of this in secret."
"Alternately, you could mobilize Mr. Greiser and his men to take care of the situation in secret."
"You are right. Let's detain her immediately."
entradas.menu: "You are right. Let's detain her immediately."

entradas.text: "Good. Let's detain her. And Petr, too -- this was all his fault."
entradas.menu: "Good. Let's detain her. And Petr, too -- this was all his fault."

entradas.text: "No, no. I'd rather do it all above board."
entradas.menu: "No, no. I'd rather do it all above board."

entradas.text: "Yes, brilliant. Let's do that."
entradas.menu: "Yes, brilliant. Let's do that."

entradas.text: "No, no. I'd rather do it all above board."
entradas.menu: "No, no. I'd rather do it all above board."

entradas.text: "Detention without trial sounds like the easiest thing to do."
entradas.menu: "Detention without trial sounds like the easiest thing to do."

entradas.text: "Let's use Karl. The fewer loose ends, the better."
entradas.menu: "Let's use Karl. The fewer loose ends, the better."

entradas.text: "No, no. I'd rather do it all above board."
entradas.menu: "No, no. I'd rather do it all above board."

entradas.text: "Then you'd -- what, exactly? Knowingly let her return to Rumburg? That would damage us even further if the truth got out."
"There are other options."
"Asking Mr. Koronti for help would be advisable, but you'll still have to do a fair amount of crisis management yourself. Unless you opt to handle this another way."
"That's why you must let Mr. Vectern take the fall."
"You must remain in control of the narrative, Mr. President. Starting by letting Petr Vectern take the fall."
"Starting by letting Petr Vectern take the fall."
"No. No, I told you, Petr did nothing wrong!"
entradas.menu: "No. No, I told you, Petr did nothing wrong!"

entradas.text: "I know his actions were problematic..."
entradas.menu: "I know his actions were problematic..."

entradas.text: "This is my fault as much as his. I should have suspected something."
entradas.menu: "This is my fault as much as his. I should have suspected something."

entradas.text: "I know you think you'd be a better vice president. But enough is enough."
entradas.menu: "I know you think you'd be a better vice president. But enough is enough."

entradas.text: "You can share the blame, but you have to prepare for your public opinion to nosedive."
entradas.menu: "You can share the blame, but you have to prepare for your public opinion to nosedive."

entradas.text: "Thankfully, Mr. Koronti can soften that blow."

"Mr. Vectern put you in danger by failing to order a background check on your closest personal staff. He betrayed your confidence to a woman with whom he was committing adultery. Anton, would you do the same to your so-called best friend?"
"Problematic is an understatement."
"I-- no. I wouldn't."
entradas.menu: "I-- no. I wouldn't."

entradas.text: "Mr. President, rest assured this is not about me."
"But please, take a moment to think about this."
"For a woman I loved? Maybe I would!"
entradas.menu: "For a woman I loved? Maybe I would!"

entradas.text: "I don't know. I can't put myself in his shoes."
entradas.menu: "I don't know. I can't put myself in his shoes."

entradas.text: I thought about how useful she'd been to me as a secretary.
"Try guzzling half a bottle of whiskey. That might help."
Lucian sighed.
"If you say so, sir. Are you ready to let Mr. Vectern take the fall?"
"If you say so, sir. Are you ready to let Mr. Vectern take the fall?"
"If you say so, sir. Are you ready to let Mr. Vectern take the fall?"
"I am your chief strategist. I have advised you on what I believe is the best strategy. But of course, the ultimate decision is yours."
"I will shoulder the blame along with him."
entradas.menu: "I will shoulder the blame along with him."

entradas.text: "All right. Petr will be our scapegoat."
entradas.menu: "All right. Petr will be our scapegoat."

entradas.text: "I will blame Livia -- I mean, Ilana -- and nobody else."
entradas.menu: "I will blame Livia -- I mean, Ilana -- and nobody else."

entradas.text: Lucian looked as if he was about to object one last time, but instead smiled thinly.
"Very well. I shall consult with our friend Mr. Koronti and write a statement for you to read at the press conference. I'll leave you to handle Miss Vance."
"Very well. I shall write a statement for you to read at the press conference. I'll leave you to handle Miss Vance."
"With pleasure."
entradas.menu: "With pleasure."

entradas.text: "Thank you."
entradas.menu: "Thank you."

entradas.text: "Of course, sir."
"Great. Let's detain her immediately."
entradas.menu: "Great. Let's detain her immediately."

entradas.text: "Great. Let's detain both her and Petr. He got us into this mess, after all."
entradas.menu: "Great. Let's detain both her and Petr. He got us into this mess, after all."

entradas.text: "Of course, sir."
"A wise choice, sir."
"By 'take care of', you mean secretly arrest, right?"
entradas.menu: "By 'take care of', you mean secretly arrest, right?"

entradas.text: "By 'take care of', you mean 'take care of for good', right?"
entradas.menu: "By 'take care of', you mean 'take care of for good', right?"

entradas.text: "I think you know precisely what I mean."
"What else could I have meant?"
"I think you know precisely what I mean."
"It means whatever you want it to mean, sir."
Lucian nodded and walked out.
"Uh, nothing."
entradas.menu: "Uh, nothing."

entradas.text: "Nothing..."
entradas.menu: "Nothing..."

entradas.text: "Kill, perhaps? It's been done before."
entradas.menu: "Kill, perhaps? It's been done before."

entradas.text: "I see. Curious that I wasn't informed."
"Kill, maybe?"
entradas.menu: "Kill, maybe?"

entradas.text: "If made to look like an accident, another covert assassination could solve our problem before it even starts. But I understand if you still harbor fond feelings for Miss Vance."
I could almost see the gears in Lucian's head turning.
"Let's just have her arrested, okay?"
entradas.menu: "Let's just have her arrested, okay?"

entradas.text: "Let's just have her arrested -- and Petr, too, while we're at it. He's done enough harm to this administration."
entradas.menu: "Let's just have her arrested -- and Petr, too, while we're at it. He's done enough harm to this administration."

entradas.text: "Screw Liv--Ilana. Let's have her killed."
entradas.menu: "Screw Liv--Ilana. Let's have her killed."

entradas.text: "Screw Miss Vance. And Petr too! Let's have them both killed."
entradas.menu: "Screw Miss Vance. And Petr too! Let's have them both killed."

entradas.text: "As you wish. I'll call Mr. Greiser right away. It ought to be done by the end of today."
"As you wish. I'll call Mr. Greiser right away. It ought to be done by the end of today."
Lucian was trying very hard not to appear pleased.
Lucian was trying very hard not to appear pleased.
"As you wish. I'll call Mr. Greiser right away. It ought to be done by the end of today."
"As you wish. I'll call Mr. Greiser right away. It ought to be done by the end of today."
Lucian was trying very hard not to appear pleased.
"As you wish. I'll call Mr. Greiser right away."
"As you wish. I'll call Mr. Greiser right away."
I called Karl Greiser from my desk and explained the situation. After a few minutes, I rang for Livia.
"Is there something you need, Mr. President?"
She entered my office.
"You tell me... Ilana."
entradas.menu: "You tell me... Ilana."

entradas.text: "It's been a pleasure working with you, Livia."
entradas.menu: "It's been a pleasure working with you, Livia."

entradas.text: "Yes. I need you to stop pretending."
entradas.menu: "Yes. I need you to stop pretending."

entradas.text: "Please, sit down."
entradas.menu: "Please, sit down."

entradas.text: A barely perceptible flash of fear crossed her face.
"Livia, sir. My name is Livia."
A barely perceptible flash of fear crossed her face.
"Wh-what do you mean, sir?"
A barely perceptible flash of fear crossed her face. She sat.
"Why did you call me in here, sir?"
I nodded toward my office doorway. Karl Greiser was standing there along with two of his guards, blocking the entrance.
"Ilana Vance, you are under arrest on suspicion of espionage. Please come with me."
Her eyes darted around the room.
"What the hell is going on? Mr. President, have you let Lucian get to your head? I thought you were smarter than that."
"You're going to pay for your lies, Ilana."
entradas.menu: "You're going to pay for your lies, Ilana."

entradas.text: "You're going to pay for the way you used Petr."
entradas.menu: "You're going to pay for the way you used Petr."

entradas.text: "I'm sorry it had to come to this."
entradas.menu: "I'm sorry it had to come to this."

entradas.text: "If you thought I wouldn't trust my closest advisor, you're the stupid one."
entradas.menu: "If you thought I wouldn't trust my closest advisor, you're the stupid one."

entradas.text: Karl's men grabbed her arms and began dragging her out.
"No. No! You can't do this to me!"
"Liv? What in the hell!? Anton, what's going on?"
Petr, hearing her cries, rushed out of his office.
"Her name's Ilana. Lucian was right about her. She's a spy."
entradas.menu: "Her name's Ilana. Lucian was right about her. She's a spy."

entradas.text: "She was using you all along, Petr."
entradas.menu: "She was using you all along, Petr."

entradas.text: "Livia, tell Petr who you really are."
entradas.menu: "Livia, tell Petr who you really are."

entradas.text: I said nothing. Petr ran up to my now ex-secretary.
entradas.menu: Say nothing.

entradas.text: "I won't say another word without a lawyer present."
She looked Petr square in the eye.
"Except this. You're a sad old drunk and a lousy lay."
"No. That can't be true. Can it? Liv?"
"Liv! Come on, tell them this was all a misunderstanding."
"Honestly, if I *were* a Rumburg spy, I'd barely have to do a thing. You two have Sordland ripe for the taking."
She straightened up, ran a hand through her curls and allowed Karl to lead her away.
Petr sank to the floor in front of me.
"Thank you, Lucian."
entradas.menu: "Thank you, Lucian."

entradas.text: "No, I'll do it myself."
entradas.menu: "No, I'll do it myself."

entradas.text: Lucian nodded and walked out.
I waited a few minutes, then rang for Livia.
"No lawyers, ma'am. You're going away for a very long time."
"Fine. Then I will say this."
She looked Petr square in the eye.
"You're a sad old drunk and a lousy lay."
"Honestly, if I *were* a Rumburg spy, I'd barely have to do a thing. You two have Sordland ripe for the taking."
Lucian nodded and walked out.
"Tell him to make her suffer."
entradas.menu: "Tell him to make her suffer."

entradas.text: "Tell him to make it painless."
entradas.menu: "Tell him to make it painless."

entradas.text: "Thank you."
entradas.menu: "Thank you."

entradas.text: "Keep me informed."
entradas.menu: "Keep me informed."

entradas.text: I took a minute to gather my thoughts, then headed out the office. My secretary was outside, typing up some correspondence at her desk.
"Stepping out for lunch. Hold my calls."
entradas.menu: "Stepping out for lunch. Hold my calls."

entradas.text: "I'm sorry again for the misunderstanding with Lucian. You've got a brilliant career ahead of you."
entradas.menu: "I'm so sorry for the misunderstanding with Lucian. You've got a brilliant career ahead of you."

entradas.text: "Thank you for your hard work, Miss Suno."
entradas.menu: "Thank you for your hard work, Miss Suno."

entradas.text: I said nothing as I walked past her.
entradas.menu: Say nothing.

entradas.text: She looked at me a bit strangely.
"Thank you, Mr. President."
"Very well, Mr. President."
She looked at me a bit strangely.
"No trouble at all, Mr. President."
I took one long, last look at her.
"Tell him to make them suffer."
entradas.menu: "Tell him to make them suffer."

entradas.text: "Tell him to make it painless."
entradas.menu: "Tell him to make it painless."

entradas.text: Lucian nodded and walked out.
"Thank you, Lucian."
entradas.menu: "Thank you, Lucian."

entradas.text: "No, I'll do it myself."
entradas.menu: "No, I'll do it myself."

entradas.text: "Anton... what the hell just happened?"
How could I tell him that the worst was still yet to come?
"Thank you."
entradas.menu: "Thank you."

entradas.text: "Keep me informed."
entradas.menu: "Keep me informed."

entradas.text: I took a minute to gather my thoughts, then left the room, taking my bottle of Erlory Maroon whiskey with me. My secretary was outside, typing up some correspondence at her desk.
Petr was about to receive some very unpleasant news.
I knocked on the door, and Petr answered. He looked at the bottle of whiskey, then at me.
"Hello there, you two. What's the occasion?"
"Life, my friend. Life."
entradas.menu: "Life, my friend. Life."

entradas.text: "Surviving your affair without a scandal, of course."
entradas.menu: "Surviving your affair without a scandal, of course."

entradas.text: "Do I need an occasion to have a drink with my friend?"
entradas.menu: "Do I need an occasion to have a drink with my friend?"

entradas.text: "I just found this. Forgot I still had it left over from my first day in office."
entradas.menu: "I just found this. Forgot I still had it left over from my first day in office."

entradas.text: "Anton, it's 11:30 in the morning."
He cracked a smile.
"What are we waiting for?"
He brought out two glasses, and I filled them up. We drank in silence for a moment.
"Lucian was right. I've been a miserable excuse for a vice president. But I'm ready to start over."
"No more affairs. No more being late. No more -- well, less drinking."
"I just want to do right by you, Anton. As a colleague and as a friend."
"I'm sorry. It's too late."
entradas.menu: "I'm sorry. It's too late."

entradas.text: "Thank you. I'm sure you will."
entradas.menu: "Thank you. I'm sure you will."

entradas.text: "You don't need to make it up to me. Our friendship goes too deep for that:"
entradas.menu: "You don't need to make it up to me. Our friendship goes too deep for that:"

entradas.text: "We'll see."
entradas.menu: "We'll see."

entradas.text: "But--"
Petr's eyes had that old sparkle in them again.
"I'm going back to work now."
entradas.menu: "I'm going back to work now."

entradas.text: "Goodbye, Petr."
entradas.menu: "Goodbye, Petr."

entradas.text: I walked out, leaving the bottle on his desk.
I returned home that evening and headed straight to my study, waiting for Karl to call.
"Are you sure about this?"
entradas.menu: "Are you sure about this?"

entradas.text: "Here. It's all in the report from our intelligence officers."
"It's okay, Lucian. I know exactly what you mean."
entradas.menu: "It's okay, Lucian. I know exactly what you mean."

entradas.text: "Have a nice one, old friend."
entradas.menu: "Have a nice one, old friend."

entradas.text: I headed down the hall to Petr's office.
entradas.menu: Head to Petr's office.

entradas.text: I headed outside with the bottle.
entradas.menu: Head out.

entradas.text: "Come to my office. You're making a scene out here."
entradas.menu: "Come to my office. You're making a scene out here."

entradas.text: "I'll tell you in my office. Feel free to take a moment first."
entradas.menu: "I'll tell you in my office. Feel free to take a moment first."

entradas.text: Once Petr was in my office, I shut the door and explained everything Lucian had told me about Livia.
"And you believed him? Well, better safe than sorry, especially after what she called me..."
"At least we finally have this ordeal behind us. Let's get on with running the country, shall we?"
"Yes, let's."
entradas.menu: "Yes, let's."

entradas.text: "Yes, let's. But first, a drink."
entradas.menu: "Yes, let's. But first, a drink."

entradas.text: "Actually, I have to tell you something..."
entradas.menu: "Actually, I have to tell you something..."

entradas.text: "Yeah? What is it?"
"Lucian wants you to resign."
entradas.menu: "Lucian wants you to resign."

entradas.text: "I want you to resign."
entradas.menu: "I want you to resign."

entradas.text: "Lucian wanted you to resign, but I told him it's not happening."
entradas.menu: "Lucian wanted you to resign, but I told him it's not happening."

entradas.text: Petr looked up at me. His expression was numb.
"You look like shit. Why don't you take the rest of the day off?"
entradas.menu: "You look like shit. Why don't you take the rest of the day off?"

entradas.text: Petr looked at me gratefully.
"Thanks, Anton. I do need a little time. But I promise it's going to be a whole new me from now on."
I watched him leave.
A whole new vice president... I didn't have the heart to tell Petr how right he was.
A whole new Petr... I hoped he was right about that.
"I... I guess I deserve this, don't I?"
"Yes. Your philandering put all of us in danger."
entradas.menu: "Yes. Your philandering put all of us in danger."

entradas.text: "No. But we need someone to take the fall for this scandal, or the administration suffers."
entradas.menu: "No. But we need someone to take the fall for this scandal, or the administration suffers."

entradas.text: He exhaled slowly. I could see tears in his eyes.
"I'm so sorry, Anton. I was never cut out for this job."
"It was fun while it lasted."
entradas.menu: "It was fun while it lasted."

entradas.text: "You really weren't. But at least you got a nice house out of the deal."

entradas.text: Petr looked up at me with an indignant expression.
"Of course he does, that fink. Did you tell him off?"
"Actually, I agree with him. I'm announcing your resignation, Petr."
entradas.menu: "Actually, I agree with him. I'm announcing your resignation, Petr."

entradas.text: "I did. We're laying this all at Rumburg's feet."

entradas.text: Petr looked up at me in surprise.
"Really, Anton? That means a lot."
Petr's face fell. He seemed to sink into the couch.
"We're laying this all at Rumburg's feet."

entradas.text: "This is as much my fault as it is yours. The administration will take the hit."

entradas.text: Petr eagerly nodded, then thought better of it and shook his head.
"No. My drunken idiocy got us into this mess in the first place."
"It's going to be a whole new me from now on, Anton. I promise."
"I can't believe I was so careless."
"That's... wow. I can't believe you'd do that for me."
"Oof. I hope they don't take it as a sign to escalate. But, wow, thanks for protecting me from Guillotine Galade over there."
"Unless Evelyn takes it in the divorce."
"Sure was, old buddy."
"You'll have some time before the news goes public. I suggest you get your affairs in order."
entradas.menu: "You'll have some time before the news goes public. I suggest you get your affairs in order."

entradas.text: "Stay for a drink."

entradas.text: "All right, I get the message. But first..."
"You did great. Sordland's just not ready for a vice president like you yet."
entradas.menu: "You did great. Sordland's just not ready for a vice president like you yet."

entradas.text: "Don't patronize me."
"We'll have some time before the news goes public. We should get our stories straight."

entradas.text: "Stay for a drink."

entradas.text: Without waiting for him to answer, I poured some whiskey into a glass. Petr grabbed the bottle instead.
"To new beginnings."
He drained a third of the bottle in one long swig, then got to his feet and unsteadily made his way to the door.
He grabbed the bottle of Erlory Maroon 30-Year-Old from the shelf behind my desk.
I knew this was for the best. But I hoped my friend would be all right.
"Sure, of course."

"If made to look like an accident, a covert assassination by your Secret State Police could solve our problem before it even starts. But I understand if you still harbor fond feelings for Miss Vance."
